title: Evaluation mode and checking
summary: model.eval switches training-sensitive layers to evaluation behaviour. Use it with no_grad when making ordinary evaluation predictions.
introduction: model.eval switches training-sensitive layers to evaluation behaviour. Use it with no_grad when making ordinary evaluation predictions. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: model.eval switches training-sensitive layers to evaluation behaviour. Use it with no_grad when making ordinary evaluation predictions.

blocks.code:
import torch

model = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(1, 1))
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    result = model(torch.tensor([[3.0]]))
print(tuple(result.shape))
blocks.title: Evaluation mode and checking

blocks.text: The shape is (1, 1). This model is untrained; the example shows the evaluation procedure, not an accurate prediction.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: eval does not train a model and does not by itself disable gradients.
